Lentil soup is the kind of dish that rewards a little patience, and this version builds flavour slowly, starting with onions cooked gently until they turn sweet and golden.

Add the carrots, celery, and garlic, then the rinsed lentils, a bay leaf, and enough stock to cover everything by a few centimetres, and let it all simmer quietly.

After about forty minutes the lentils will have softened, and you can blend half of the soup for a creamier texture, leaving the rest whole for a little bite.

Finish with lemon juice, olive oil, and plenty of black pepper, and serve with crusty bread, which is honestly the best part of the whole meal.
